page: Microsoft Azure D16d_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. It is driven by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at a base clock frequency of 2.6 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance allocates 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. System memory totals 64.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware vector support includes AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI, alongside AES cryptographic acceleration.

A defining hardware feature of the D16d_v4 is its bundled local storage array, offering 644 GB of direct-attached solid-state drive capacity. This integrated ephemeral storage provides high-speed scratch space without incurring extra storage attach costs. Graphic processing units are absent on this instance, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default. The cache hierarchy provisions a 32 KB L1 data cache and 1.0 MB L2 cache per core alongside a shared 35 MB L3 cache pool.

Benchmark metrics demonstrate mid-tier performance across varied computational tasks. The instance achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 7,845 and a single-core score of 1,271. In stress-ng tests, multi-core throughput registered at 14,893.66, whereas single-core testing fell into the lower quartile at 1,412.78. Memory bandwidth shows solid throughput, measuring 80.99 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 43.83 GB/sec for uncached writes. Operational benchmarks highlight 13.99 million Redis SET operations per second and 11.82 GB/sec static web serving throughput.

The resource profile makes the D16d_v4 cost-efficient for applications requiring balanced processing coupled with rapid local temporary I/O. Primary workload fits include mid-tier relational databases, in-memory caching solutions like Redis, continuous integration and compilation pipelines, and containerized web serving. Tradeoffs involve restrained single-thread clock performance and modest prompt processing throughput for large language models.
description: Microsoft Azure D16d_v4 is a balanced general-purpose instance featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical Intel Xeon 8272CL cores at 2.6 GHz. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V on x86_64 architecture, it delivers 64.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a 4.0 GB per core balance. The configuration includes 644 GB of integrated local SSD storage, rendering it well-suited for I/O-intensive ephemeral storage needs without extra attached volume expenses, though it lacks dedicated GPUs. Benchmark results position the machine solidly in the mid-range, reaching a Geekbench multi-core score of 7,845, a PassMark CPU score of 15,473.34, and 13.99 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-core metrics remain modest, with stress-ng single-core performance scoring in the bottom quartile. The instance offers balanced hardware economics for enterprise web serving, Redis caching tiers, code compilation pipelines, and operational database workloads that profit from direct-attached NVMe-class storage.
